ds: Virtual asset kiosks let users convert cash to crypto with light verification, making them attractive for scam victims forced to pay and for criminals placing cash. Risk centres on structuring, repeated high-value use, third-party direction and destination wallets tied to scams or mixers.

src.t: FinCEN, Notice on Scams Involving Convertible Virtual Currency Kiosks (2025)
FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)

cn.rt: Hard call: kiosk is outside the bank, but scam victims coached by phone withdraw cash or cash-advance to feed kiosks; visible as unusual cash withdrawals and transfers.

rat: Cash-to-crypto kiosks used by scam victims and for placement.

ind.n: Repeated cash deposits just below ID or reporting thresholds
ind.cx: The same user or phone number uses a kiosk several times in a short period at sizes below verification tiers.
ind.fp: Frequent small purchases by regular users.
ind.ds: Repeated cash deposits kept just under a reporting, identification or monitoring threshold.
ind.cn: Cash deposits just below reporting or identification threshold

ind.n: Multiple users sending to the same destination wallet
ind.cx: Many different kiosk customers direct funds to one address.
ind.ds: Many different customers send to or whitelist the same external address.
ind.cn: Same external wallet used by multiple unrelated customers

ind.n: Older customer on first use with large amounts
ind.cx: First-time, elderly user deposits large sums, often on a phone call, consistent with scam coercion.
ind.ds: First-time, elderly user deposits large sums, often on a phone call, consistent with scam coercion.

ind.n: Destination wallet linked to scam or fraud clusters
ind.cx: Receiving address is attributed to investment, romance or impersonation scams.
ind.ds: Receiving address is attributed to investment, romance or impersonation scams.

ind.n: Use of multiple kiosks across locations in one day
ind.cx: User travels between machines to avoid limits or detection.
ind.ds: User travels between machines to avoid limits or detection.

ind.n: Shared phone number or ID across unrelated transactions
ind.cx: Same identifiers appear for apparently unrelated users or reused after refusal.
ind.ds: Same phone, email, address, device or ID number appears across multiple unrelated customers or users.

ind.n: Kiosk placed in high-risk locations without monitoring
ind.cx: Machines in venues with weak oversight show disproportionate high-risk activity.
ind.ds: Machines in venues with weak oversight show disproportionate high-risk activity.

ind.n: Customer on phone while transacting or reading from instructions
ind.cx: Staff or footage note user following directions while depositing cash.
ind.fp: Customer using a guide or helper.
ind.ds: Customer is on an active phone call, hesitant or following dictated instructions while depositing cash or making an online payment.
ind.cn: Customer on a live call while transacting

ind.n: Cash from bulk notes in poor condition or unusual denominations
ind.cx: Large volumes of small or bundled notes deposited in sequence.
ind.ds: Large volumes of small or bundled notes deposited in sequence.

ind.cx: Operator fails to monitor wallets, refunds or complaints, allowing patterns to persist.
ind.ds: Operator fails to monitor wallets, refunds or complaints, allowing patterns to persist.

ctl.ds: Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.

Caps transaction size, frequency, load, withdrawal and deposit values, with staged increases as legitimate behaviour is established and per-customer limits at kiosks. It bounds the loss and laundering capacity of new or higher-risk accounts.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Duplicate and synthetic identity checks at onboarding
ctl.ds: Compares new applicant identifiers such as name, email, phone, address, device and bank account with existing customers, previously declined or exited applicants and known-bad data. Matches are blocked or referred, limiting repeat applicants, synthetic identities and mule recruitment.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Risk appetite and product policy statements
ctl.ds: Documents the institution's appetite and permitted or prohibited products, assets and activities for a given risk area, with limits and review cadence. It gives staff and systems a clear boundary for acceptance.

Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.
